subject: CColModel actual allocation size discrepancy — 56 bytes vs. 48 bytes claimed

finding.description: A Capstone disassembly of the function at 0x537490 (which attaches a CColModel to a CBaseModelInfo entry during model loading) reveals a `push 0x38` immediately before a call to the memory allocator at 0x531AE0. This means CColModel is being allocated as 0x38 = 56 bytes, not 0x30 = 48 bytes as documented in disassembly.

proof_sequence: 0x5374DB: cmp word ptr [ebp + 0x10], bx   ; check if model already has a colmodel
0x5374DF: je 0x537546                      ; if already assigned, skip allocation
0x5374F7: mov ecx, eax                      ; ecx = newly allocated CColModel*

first_instructions: 0x59DE01: mov esi, ecx           ; ecx = this pointer (the newly allocated block)
0x59DE08: mov dword ptr [esi], 0x866e78  ; set vtable pointer

impact.schema_difference: Our SASDK schema for CColModel (C6) documents 5 fields totaling 48 bytes. The exe allocates 56 bytes. The 8-byte gap (offsets 48-55) contains undocumented fields.

possible_extra_fields.description: Unknown — may be a padding word, a CColDataVolume* extension, or a triangle count for COL4 format
Unknown — may be a reference count or link pointer

impact.action: The CColModel schema needs a Capstone sweep of CColModel member functions to identify what code accesses offsets 48-55.
impact.capstone_target: CColModel::RemoveCollisionVolumes, CColModel::ReleaseData, CColModel::SetLink — any of these will access the mystery bytes
